sentences.text: Shri D.S. Pawar and Shri Sanjay K. Dwivedi, learned counsel for the applicants.
Shri K.N. Gupta learned Senior Counsel assisted by Shri Kunal Suryavanshi and Ms. Ayushi Pophali, learned counsel for the respondent no.1/Official Liquidator.
Shri Mukesh Sharma, learned counsel for the respondent/F.S.Advertisers.

Shri K.C. Verma and Shri U.K. Shrivas, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the employees of J.C.
Mill/Union.
Shri Deepak Khot Govt. Advocate for the respondent/State.
Heard on I.A. No. 1076 of 2023 and OLR No. 1/2023.

I.A No. 1076 of 2023 has been preferred by the State Government seeking necessary direction/permission from this Court for acquiring land bearing Survey Nos. 420 and 425 situated at Patwari Halka Gospura at Tahsil, Gwalior recorded in the name of company under liquidation.

In the application, it has been mentioned that vide order dated 25.01.2022, Collector, Gwalior had alloted land bearing Survey No. 474 ad- measuring 0.199 hectares in favour of Rail Vikas Nigam for carrying out a special Rail project meant for the State of U.P., Rajasthan and M.P. for construction of railway line which is approved/declared as Mathura-Jhansi, third line (273.4 Kms.)

Since the remaining area comes under owner ship of the Company under the liquidation, vide letter dated 25.10.2021, Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd., Gwalior had requested Collector, Gwalior- cum- Land Acquisition Officer for acquiring the said land being survey Nos. 420 and 425, ad-measuring 0.02 hectares by invoking the provisions of Section 40 (Urgency Clause) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (herein after referred to as 'Act of 2013').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
In the application it has further been averred that Rail Vikas Nigam,
Ltd., Gwalior had calculated the estimated compensation for the desired area ad-measuring 0.02 hectares of land considering the guideline value of the said land for the years 2022-21 and had M/S.J.C.Mills Ltd. vs B.I.F.R. on 8 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119728553/
1 deposited Rs. 24, 33, 760/- with Collector -Cum-Land- Acquisition Officer and by way of the present application seeks permission/leave of this Court to proceed with the acquisition proceedings of area ad-measuring 0.02 hectares of land out of Survey Nos. 420 and 425 which is recorded in the name of company under liquidation and is in possession of the Official Liquidator appointed by this Court.

Similar fact has been mentioned by the Official Liquidator in OLR No. 1/2023 wherein in para '6' it is stated that objections for acquisition of the aforesaid land were called in the office from the Stake Holders vide its letter dated 26.12.2022 and the date for submission of the objections was fixed as 28.12.2022.

Though, in the OLR there is no mention of the fact that any objections were received from anyone, but the learned Senior Counsel, Shri Gupta appearing on behalf of the Official Liquidator stated at bar that no objections were received even after issuance of the notices to the Stake Holders.

It was further mentioned in the OLR that a letter dated 26.12.2022 was issued to the District Collector-cum-Land Acquisition Officer informing him that a part of land bearing Survey No. 420 and 425 belonging to the company under liquidation, cannot be acquired/transferred without prior approval of the Company Court as contemplated u/s. 446 of the Companies Act.

Learned Counsel for the State as well as learned Senior Counsel for the Official Liquidator submits that so far as acquisition part is concerned no objections had been raised either by any stake holder nor the Official Liquidator has any objection under whose possession the land is at present.

Learned Senior Counsel though submits that since the land the land is to be used for a public purpose for laying down a new railway line running between Jhansi and Mathura, therefore, there is no objection with regard to the acquisition of the said land, however, the objection is with regard to the amount of compensation which has been calculated by the State.

It has been submitted that calculation is to be made as per Rule 273 of the Companies (Court) Rules 1959 which lays down as under: -
"273. Procedure at
sale.-Every

sale shall be held by the Official Liquidator, or, if the Judge shall so direct, by an agent or an auctioneer approved by the Court, and subject to such terms and conditions, if any, as may be approved by the Court.
All sales shall be made by public auction or by inviting sealed tenders or in such manners as the Judge may direct."

;
and it has been submitted by him that amount which has been calculated by the State is just an estimate and has not been calculated as per procedure laid down under the Companies Rules as well as under the Act of 2013.

On the other hand, Shri Khot appearing for the State submits that the compensation has been calculated as per the Act of 2013 and amount of Rs. 24,33,760/- has been calculated on an estimated basis and would attain finality once the final award is passed and if the Official Liquidator has any objection with regard to the quantum of amount, he can very well approach the Land Acquisition Officer/Competent Authority and raise the objections as provided under the Act of 2013.

2
Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the record.
It appears that though land acquisition proceedings have been initiated by the State Government, but till date no final award has been passed.

Since it is an admitted legal position that Right to Fair Compensation Act, 2013 being a special Act would prevail upon the Companies Act and rules framed thereunder being a general law, the compensation which is to be calculated would be as per the procedure prescribed under the Act of 2013.
Therefore the objection taken by learned Senior Counsel with regard to the calculation of the compensation as per provisions of Company (Court) Rules, 1959, cannot be sustained.
As and when the final award is passed, the Official Liquidator would be at liberty to challenge the same if at all he is aggrieved by calculation/quantum as per the provision of the Act of 2013.

As the provisions of Section 40 of the Act of 2013 has been invoked by the State Government for acquisition of land bearing Survey Nos. 420 and 425, and as per the provisions of Section 40 (3), it is incumbent upon the Land Acquisition Officer to deposit 80% of the estimated amount determined towards the compensation, is directed to be paid to the Official Liquidator, before taking possession.

Accordingly, this Court while allowing the application I.A. No. 1076 of 2023 permits and directs the State Government to acquire the land bearing Survey Nos. 420 and 425 ad-measuring 0.02 hectares, and the Official Liquidator in turn is also directed to hand over the possession to the State Government.

Hearing on I.A. No. 2223 of 2023 and part of OLR No. 1/2023 which is in regard to payment of remaining amount to ex-workers on the request of learned Senior Counsel Shri Gupta is deferred till next date of hearing.
List the case on 25th of July, 2023.
